topic: Rear wiper stopped moving? Don't assume the motor's dead yet.

beats.vo: Rear wiper stopped moving? Don't assume the motor's dead yet.
beats.visual: Macro shot of a rear windshield wiper arm resting against dark tinted glass, static camera, overcast exterior light

beats.vo: Most rear wiper failures aren't the motor at all — it's a blown fuse, and it usually has its own, separate from the front.
beats.visual: Close-up of a vehicle interior fuse box panel, rows of colored fuses in focus, static camera, no hand in frame

beats.vo: Check the fuse box first. If it's blown, that's a five-minute fix, not a motor replacement.
beats.visual: Extreme macro push-in on a single pulled fuse in a small fixture, showing the blown metal element inside

beats.vo: If the fuse is fine but you hear a hum with no movement, that points to the linkage or motor — that one needs a look.
beats.visual: Interior shot looking into the open rear hatch trim area where a wiper motor linkage sits, dim ambient garage light, static camera

beats.vo: Worth checking the fuse before you assume the worst. Stop by and we'll take a look.
